identityReview: Shavkat Miromonovich Mirziyoyev, born 24 July 1957, Zaamin District, Jizzakh. Current Uzbek president; earlier regional executive, academic and prime minister. Candidate of Technical Sciences preserved from Russian official biography without unsupported degree-year/equivalence. Temporary presidential authority September 2016 differs from December election and formal inauguration. Five-year 2021 term superseded by constitutional reset and 2023 seven-year term; no guaranteed future mandate.
lifeStatusEvidence: The original presidential press-service account dated 17 November 2026 reports his actual restricted and expanded Muscat talks with Sultan Haitham. This is a completed meeting, not the earlier state-visit itinerary. Dunyo repeats the press-service account and is treated as dependent corroboration.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read government biography, official Russian/English degree descriptions, selected IMF 2019 exchange-rate annex and 2018 staff statement, ILO 2021-harvest findings announcement, CEC election results, ODIHR preliminary statement plus selected final-report context/results, actual 2023 inauguration and 2026 Muscat meeting records. Read Commons root and both crops, historical source-review notice and current presidential footer; Facebook source inaccessible.
corrections: Read government biography: born 24 July 1957, Zaamin District in Jizzakh; 1981 mechanical-engineering graduation and institute research/teaching/vice-rector work. Mirzo Ulugbek district head in 1992, Jizzakh 1996–2001, Samarkand 2001–2003, premiership from 2003 with confirmations 2005/2010/2015. Parliamentary and executive roles overlap. Temporary presidential powers assigned by joint parliamentary resolution 8 September 2016; election 4 December, formal office 14 December, official share 88.61%. Re-election 24 October 2021 reported as 80.1%, then five-year term. The biography stops detailed election chronology at 2021 despite a 2026 update label; 2023 changes are supplied separately. Promotional praise is not independent impact evidence.

Read official Russian biography alongside English version. Russian explicitly says Candidate of Technical Sciences and docent; English translates the degree as PhD. Profile preserves the original degree designation without inventing an award year, US degree equivalence, higher Doctor of Sciences or current teaching appointment. Mechanical engineering, agricultural irrigation institute and academic administration are distinct from later political offices.

Read selected Annex II exchange-rate section of IMF 2019 Article IV report, paragraph 15: unification and access liberalization on 5 September 2017, official rate from 4250 to 8100 sum per US dollar. Report also describes remaining capital-flow restrictions and a managed de facto exchange-rate regime. No claim of complete capital-account openness, immediate free floating or a 90% loss in currency value derived incorrectly from the quotation change. Full statistical report and charts were not exhaustively audited.

Read ILO announcement of 1 March 2022 about the 2021 cotton harvest: 11000 picker interviews, 99% voluntary and around 1% direct or perceived coercion. ILO’s systemic-elimination conclusion is retained with these limits. Reported child/adult changes over years and institutional reform are not wholly credited to the president; data do not certify all industries or 2026 conditions. Announcement preceded publication of the full report on 29 March; only announcement findings were read. A separate 29 January 2021 ILO article concerns the 2020 crop and 96% voluntary work and is not conflated with the 2021 harvest.

Read CEC results account for the 9 July 2023 early presidential election: official winner Mirziyoyev with 87.05% of voters participating. Official vote result is attributed to election authorities rather than presented as an independent certification of free competition or share of all residents. Other candidates’ shares are not needed in the profile. ODIHR’s final-report annex reproduces the same result, explicitly according to CEC data.

Read ODIHR’s 10 July 2023 observation statement: technical preparations and some legal reforms acknowledged; genuine competition absent, expression restricted, serious election-day procedural irregularities and integrity concerns observed. None of the registered candidates publicly challenged the incumbent with alternative political views. The profile attributes these judgments to observers, without portraying the official vote share as rebutting them or inventing a criminal verdict.

Read selected political-context section and final-results annex of ODIHR final report, notably printed pages 4–5 and 27. April 30 referendum and amended constitution extended presidential term from five to seven years, reset incumbent term count, and empowered early election called 8 May for 9 July. Former term was due to end in 2026; profile does not retain that as the current endpoint. Annex states 13,625,055 votes and 87.05% according to CEC. No full report/observer appendix review is claimed, and a possible future re-election is not treated as guaranteed office until 2037.

Read actual 14 July 2023 inauguration record: oath at joint parliamentary session after the 9 July election, CEC certificate and seven-year programme. Official assertion of democratic principles is not adopted over independent ODIHR assessment. GDP, investment and green-energy targets in the speech are prospective, not achieved results or personal assets.

Read presidential press service’s 17 November 2026 account of actual restricted and expanded talks with Sultan Haitham at Al Alam Palace, Muscat. Leaders announced strategic partnership and agreed a roadmap and coordination mechanism. Plans concerning investment capital, funds and projects do not prove money disbursed or construction completed. Dunyo’s same-day account corroborates publication but derives from the presidential press service, so it is not counted as an independent eyewitness source. No original meeting video or signatures were inspected.

Read IMF staff concluding statement dated 14 March 2018: September 2017 foreign-exchange liberalization and inflation pressures from exchange-rate/price changes. It is a staff mission statement, not a separate Executive Board decision. The profile does not turn forecasts for 2018–2019 into achieved outcomes or imply that liberalization had no adjustment costs.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No full IMF or ODIHR appendix audit, full ILO 2021 report reading, independent causal assessment of all reforms, current all-sector labour-rights certification, original diplomatic video, diploma inspection, Facebook licence recovery or portrait pixels. Official results and observer criticisms remain separately attributed. Investment and future policy plans are not completed outcomes.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed for Zaamin birth and 1981 mechanical engineering, original Candidate of Technical Sciences designation, overlapping regional/parliamentary roles, 2003 premiership, September acting authority versus December 2016 election/inauguration, 2021 five-year term versus 2023 seven-year reset, official 87.05% versus ODIHR competition criticism, September 2017 exchange rates 4250/8100 sum per dollar, 2021 cotton harvest announced March 2022 with 99% voluntary and 1% coercion, and actual 17 November 2026 Oman talks versus plans awaiting execution.
